{"task": {"id": "I_kwDONElfw88AAAABUhhBeg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlV6Pzg-Cv6k", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlV6P", "number": 2, "title": "Add concise Issue/PR templates and AI development/review guidance", "body": "## Problem

three-mmd-loader does not currently have the concise Issue/PR templates and AI-assisted development/review guidance used by the other ProjectWeave-managed repositories. Contributors and agents need a clear place to describe scope, expected results, validation, and review expectations without inventing a large process framework.

## Expected outcome

Add the same small set of collaboration artifacts, adapting GitWeave's current files to three-mmd-loader:

- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md`: a small template with Problem, Expected outcome, and Context.
- `.github/pull_request_template.md`: a small template with Summary, Outcome, Validation, and Related issues. Brief scope prompts are fine; avoid a long checklist.
- `docs/development-flow.md`: the default Issue → implementation → PR → review → revision → merge flow, with an emphasis on AI-assisted work.
- `docs/review-guidelines.md`: review against the source Issue for completeness, unnecessary scope, correctness, and appropriate validation.

Add a short README link so the guidance is discoverable. Write these collaboration artifacts in English. Preserve the repository's existing product, research, technical-validation, and implementation documents; adapt only genuinely necessary repository-specific details.

Follow the shared principle: prefer the smallest change that fully satisfies the Issue. An Issue defines scope; unclear requirements should be clarified rather than invented. Review must check both missing work and unjustified additions such as speculative abstractions, unrelated refactoring, or new frameworks. A PR should claim to close an Issue only when it fully addresses it; intentional partial work must be described accurately without presenting the Issue as fully resolved. Use validation appropriate to the change.

Include the completion-criteria policy already implemented in GitWeave #110 / PR #111:

> By default, completion criteria should be executable and verifiable by an AI agent. Require human checks, such as physical-device testing, subjective evaluation, or external approval, only when there is a necessary reason to do so.
>
> When human work is required, state why it is necessary and what result is expected. Distinguish optional additional validation from mandatory completion criteria.

Put that policy in the development guidance and a concise reminder plus a working local-guidance link under the Issue template's Expected outcome section. Do not require naming a human tester, and do not add a separate new policy about Issue splitting/updates. Necessary human validation remains allowed; do not weaken existing product-specific acceptance requirements or claim unperformed tests passed.

Keep this change limited to the four collaboration files and minimal README navigation. Do not add CI, bots, runtime changes, a broad coding-style guide, or a larger governance framework. Completion means the files exist, their wording is consistent with the references and repository, and the documentation links/template formatting/whitespace have been checked. No human or physical-device test is required for this documentation-only change.

## Context

Use the latest GitWeave versions as the reference rather than creating a different process:

- Issue template: https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md
- PR template: https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md
- Development flow: https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md
- Review guidelines: https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md
- Completed acceptance-guidance change: https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/issues/110 and https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/pull/111

ProjectWeave, my-audio-to-text, Refloom, and three-game-kit already have analogous templates/documents. This Issue adds the missing set to three-mmd-loader, including the same agreed completion-criteria policy. If an equivalent file appears before implementation, reuse it and add only the missing guidance rather than creating duplicates.
